baskingshark: An enormous slow plankton-straining fish drifting with its jaws opened to their fullest extent, seen in side profile. Its open jaws form a HUGE HOLLOW CIRCULAR RING, a smooth round opening as wide and as tall as its whole head, so that the front of the animal is essentially an open barrel mouth held wide with nothing but soft pale feathery combs lining the inside of that ring. The rim of the ring is smooth, plain and even all the way around, like the lip of a bucket. Behind this ring, FIVE COLOSSAL GILL SLITS encircle the head almost completely, meeting over the top of the back and again beneath the throat so the head is wrapped in five deep grooves like stacked collars. A short blunt conical nose above the ring, a small dark eye, a bulky heavy grey-brown body, a tall triangular fin on its back, and a crescent tail. Slow, harmless and gentle, straining water for plankton
walrus_c: A young pinniped pup lying on its belly, a chubby heavy-bodied baby sea mammal with THICK WRINKLED CINNAMON-BROWN SKIN falling in loose soft folds. Its face is round, plump and entirely SMOOTH-JAWED: below its nostrils it has only a DENSE DROOPING MOUSTACHE OF STIFF PALE WHISKERS covering a soft rounded whiskery upper lip that curves gently down to a small closed mouth, so its whole muzzle is a soft bristly cushion of hair and nothing harder. A domed forehead, small dark shining eyes, short broad flippers, a plump rounded body. Very young, soft and unarmed
whiterhino_c: A very young rhinoceros calf, a BABY animal of only a few months old with unmistakably infant proportions: an OVERSIZED HEAD that looks too big for its body, SHORT STUBBY LEGS, a small rounded barrel body and a soft rounded forehead. Its snout is completely SMOOTH AND ROUNDED, sloping down in one clean unbroken curve from forehead to a wide flat square grazing lip, with nothing rising from it - the top of its nose is bare, plain and smooth like the back of a spoon. Pale warm grey skin, LIGHT ALL OVER LIKE WET CEMENT, evenly and softly lit with no dark patches and no heavy shadows. Small round ears with tufted rims, a stubby tail. Clean and pale and very young
blackrhino_c: A very young rhinoceros calf seen from a THREE-QUARTER FRONT ANGLE, its head turned toward the viewer and its body angled away so both the face and one full flank show. A BABY animal of only a few months old with unmistakably infant proportions: an OVERSIZED HEAD too big for its body, SHORT STUBBY LEGS, a small rounded body and a soft rounded forehead. Its snout is completely SMOOTH AND ROUNDED, sloping in one clean unbroken curve from forehead to a POINTED HOOKED PREHENSILE UPPER LIP for browsing, with nothing rising from it - the top of its nose is bare, plain and smooth. Soft mid-grey skin, evenly lit, small tubular ears, a stubby tail
sunfishmola: A gigantic ocean sunfish seen in side profile, an animal shaped like an ENORMOUS FLAT ROUND PLATE standing on edge. ITS OUTLINE IS A CIRCLE: the distance from its back to its belly is THE SAME as the distance from its mouth to its rear, so the body forms a perfectly round disc like a dinner plate, a car wheel or a full moon, hugely deep from top to bottom and squashed flat side to side. From the top of this circle a SINGLE ENORMOUS POINTED FIN rises straight up, and from the bottom an identical one points straight down, each nearly as long as the disc is wide, giving the animal a tall vertical shape overall. THE REAR OF THE DISC SIMPLY STOPS in a short frilled scalloped rudder of skin, a wavy trailing frill flush against the body with no fin rays, no fork, no crescent and no fan. A tiny round mouth, one large round eye, small pectoral fins, rough mottled silver-grey skin
oarfish: An immensely long silver ribbon-fish hanging vertically in deep water, its body drifting in slow S-shaped waves. THE PROPORTIONS ARE THE POINT: its body is A NARROW STRAP no deeper than a person's hand is wide, yet it runs on and on for the entire height of the picture from top edge to bottom edge, at least TWENTY TIMES LONGER THAN IT IS DEEP - a strip of silver ribbon, a length of belt, a strap of foil. It is flattened side to side like a blade. The strap TAPERS AWAY SMOOTHLY TO A FINE THREAD at its lower end and simply stops there. A crimson fin of short rays runs the whole length of its back like piping along a seam. A TALL CREST OF LONG RED PLUMES rises from the top of its small blunt head, and two long red oar-shaped fins trail from just behind it. Silvery skin flecked with dark spots, one large dark eye
